4.text:
The $n/k=10/5=2$.  
For a cohesive group $S$ we need $|S|\ge \ell\,n/k$ and
$|\cap_{i\in S}A(i)|\ge\ell$ and then some $i\in S$ has
$|A(i)\cap W|\ge\ell$.

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\cap A(i)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$.
  $\ell =3$ is cohesive.  Hence some $i\in S_{x}$ has $\ge3$ approvals in $W$.
  $A(2)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{2}\},A(3)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{3}\}$ and
  $A(8\!-\!10)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\}$.  The cheapest way to give a
  voter of $S_{x}$ three approvals is $2x$’s $+y_{2}$ or $2x$’s $+z_{1}$.
  Hence at least two $x$’s, i.e. at least two candidates of
  $A(1)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, must belong to $W$.
  With $2x$’s and $y_{2}$,
  $W_{0}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
  $|A(2)\cap W_{0}|=3$ and $|A(4)\cap W_{0}|=2$.
  So $2$ candidates of $A(1)$ can be attained and $1$ is impossible.

* $S_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\cap A(i)=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $|S_{y}|=4$.
  $\ell=2$ is cohesive.  $A(4,5)=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ and
  $A(6,7)=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$ are disjoint from $A(1)$.
  Hence at least two non-$A(1)$ candidates from
  $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ are necessary in $W$.
  With $b$ non-$A(1)$ places and $a+b=5$ we have $b\ge2$, i.e. $a\le3$.

The bound is tight e.g.

$W^{*}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

$|A(1)\cap W^{*}|=3$, $|A(2)\cap W^{*}|=3$, $|A(4)\cap W^{*}|=2$,
so $S_{x}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{y}$ is $2$-represented; $W^{*}$ is
EJR and contains $3$ $A(1)$ candidates.  No EJR committee can contain
$4$ $A(1)$ candidates because $b=1$ would give the voters $4\!-\!7$ at most
one approval.

Hence in an EJR $5$-committee voter $1$ can be represented by $2$ to $3$
candidates, the minimum being $2$ and the maximum being $3$.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: H. min 2, max 3

2.text:
Voter 1 approves $V_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and the committee has
$|C|=5$, $n=10$, $k=5$ so $n/k=2$.

For the $A$–cluster $S_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ we have $|S_{A}|=6$ and
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{A}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.   EJR with $\ell =3$
needs a voter of $S_{A}$ with $\ge 3$ approvals.  For $v\in S_{A}$

* $v=1:\;|C\cap A_{1}|=c_{x}+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}=a$,
* $v=2,3:\;|C\cap A_{v}|=c_{x}+{\bf1}_{y_{v}}$,
* $v=8,9,10:\;|C\cap A_{v}|=c_{x}+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}$,
where $c_{x}=|C\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$ and $a=c_{x}+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$
is the number of $V_{1}$-candidates in $C$.

For the $B$–cluster $S_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ we have
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{B}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and $|S_{B}|=4$.
EJR with $\ell =2$ requires a voter of $S_{B}$ with $\ge2$ approvals.
$A_{i}\cap V_{1}=\varnothing$ for $i\in S_{B}$, hence only the
$5-a$ candidates of $C\setminus V_{1}$ can help $S_{B}$.

* $a\ge4$.  $C$ then contains $4$ $V_{1}$-candidates and one
outside candidate $o$.  $|C\cap A_{1}|=a\ge4$, so $S_{A}$ is satisfied,
but every $i\in S_{B}$ can obtain at most
$|C\cap A_{i}| \le {\bf1}_{o\in A_{i}}\le1$, so the $\ell=2$ condition
for $S_{B}$ is violated.  Hence $a\le3$.

* $a=3$ is attainable.  E.g. 
$C=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
$|C\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|C\cap A_{2,3}|=3$, $|C\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
and $|C\cap A_{4,5}|=|C\cap A_{6,7}|=2$.  All EJR conditions are met
and $|C\cap V_{1}|=3$.

* $a=2$ is attainable and $a=1$ is impossible.  With $a=2$ we can take
$c_{x}=2$, ${\bf1}_{y_{1}}={\bf1}_{z_{3}}=0$.  Then $v=2$ has
$|C\cap A_{2}|=c_{x}+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}\ge3$ e.g. 
$C=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
Now $|C\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|C\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|C\cap A_{8,9,10}|=2$,
$|C\cap A_{4,5}|=|C\cap A_{6,7}|=2$, so EJR holds and
$|C\cap V_{1}|=2$.

$a=1$ would give $|C\cap A_{1}|\le1$, $|C\cap A_{2,3}|\le1+{\bf1}_{y_{v}}\le2$,
$|C\cap A_{8,9,10}|\le1+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}\le2$, so no voter of $S_{A}$ can
reach $3$ approvals.  Hence $a\ge2$.

Therefore an EJR-5-committee can contain $2$ or $3$ candidates approved
by voter 1, and both extremes are realizable.

Min $2$, Max $3$.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: H. min 2, max 3

7.text:
The $6$-voter $X$-cluster $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and $|S_{X}|=6\ge3\,n/k$.
Hence an EJR–committee has to give some $i\in S_{X}$ at least three
approved members.  The only candidates approved by the whole of $S_{X}$
are $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$, so

$$|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge 3\tag{1}$$

The $4$-voter $Y$-cluster $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2\,n/k$.
Hence some $i\in S_{Y}$ has to receive at least two approved members.
With (1) this can be done only with the two seats left after the three
$x$'s.  Write $W=X_{3}\cup R_{2}$ with $|X_{3}|=3$, $X_{3}\subset\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
For $i=4,5$, $A_{i}=Y\cup\{z_{1}\}$ and for $i=6,7$, $A_{i}=Y\cup\{z_{2}\}$.
Hence $|R_{2}\cap A_{i}|\ge2$ for some $i\in S_{Y}$ iff

* $R_{2}\subset Y$, or
* $R_{2}=\{y,z_{1}\}$ with $y\in Y$, or
* $R_{2}=\{y,z_{2}\}$ with $y\in Y$,

and in particular $R_{2}$ has to contain at least one $y\in\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
Up to renaming

$$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\cup\{y,y'\},\qquad y,y'\in Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$$

is the essentially unique EJR–type family.  In particular
$|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|=3$ and no $y_{1}$ or $z_{3}$ can be put into
$W$, otherwise the $Y$-cluster would lose its two-member representative.
Hence with the usual cohesive version of EJR

$$|W\cap A_{1}|=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}|=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|=3,$$

and the three $x$’s are forced in every EJR committee.  In particular the
number of $1$–approved members of an EJR committee is pinned down to $3$.

Min $=3$, Max $=3$, i.e. option E.

6.text:
The 7 voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 have the common set $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
For $n=10,\;k=5$ the EJR threshold is $\ell n/k =2\ell$.  
With $\ell =3$ we need a voter in $\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ with $\ge 3$
representatives.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $p={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}\in\{0,1\}$, $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.  
Voter 1 is represented by $a+p$.

* Group $\{4,5,6,7\}$ has the common set $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  
For $\ell =2$ we need

$c+\max\{{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},{\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}\}\ge 2$,

i.e. at least two $y$'s or one $y$ and a $z$ in $W$.

* For the $x$-group
$\max\!\left\{a+p,\;a+y_{2},\;a+y_{3},\;a+z_{1}\right\}\ge 3$.

Hence
$|W|=a+p+y_{2}+y_{3}+c+{\bf1}_{z_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{2}}=5$.

$c+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$ needs at least two slots outside
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  With $a+p$ approvals for voter 1

$5-a-p\ge 2$  and  $a+p\ge 3$ is forced by the $x$-group, so
$a+p\le3$.

$a=3,p=0$ and $c=2$ e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$a+p=3$ for voter 1 and satisfies
$\max_{i\in\{4\!-\!7\}}|W\cap A_{i}|=2$ and
$\max_{i\in\{1,2,3,8\!-\!10\}}|W\cap A_{i}|=3$.
Hence $3$ is attainable and $a+p=4$ would need $5-a-p\le1$, contradicting
$c+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$.  So
$\max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

The smallest feasible $a+p$ is obtained with $a=2,p=0$.  Then
$5-a-p=3$ and $a+y_{2}\ge3$ can be met with $y_{2}=1$ and $c=2$, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.

Now $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $\max_{i\in4-7}|W\cap A_{i}|=2$ and
$|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, so EJR holds.  $a+p=1$ would give
$\max\{a+p,a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+z_{1}\}\le2<3$, so $1$ is impossible.

Hence an EJR 5-committee can give voter 1 2 approvals and can give him at
most 3 approvals.

Min 2, Max 3  i.e. option H.

5.text:
With $n=10,\;k=5$ we have $n/k=2$ and a group $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.
EJR is

$\forall\ell\ge1\; \forall S\;|S|\ge2\ell,\;
|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell\Longrightarrow
\exists i\in S\;|A_{i}\cap W|\ge\ell $ .

The six voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$ have
$\bigcap_{i}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|S|=6$.
Hence $S$ is $3$-cohesive, $2$-cohesive and $1$-cohesive.
Put $G=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$.  For $i\in G$
\[
A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\},\;
A_{2}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{2}\},\;
A_{3}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{3}\},\;
A_{8,9,10}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\}.
\]
In particular $|A_{1}\cap W|=|W\cap A_{1}|=:t$.

* $ \ell=3$ on $G$ needs a voter in $G$ with $\ge3$ approvals in $W$.
$|A_{1}\cap W|=t$, so $t\ge3$ gives the condition with voter 1.
If $t=2$ the condition can still be met by voter 8, e.g. with
$2\,x$'s and $z_{1}\in W$, $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$.
With $t\le1$ we have $|A_{1}\cap W|\le1$, $|A_{2}\cap W|\le2$,
$|A_{8}\cap W|\le2$, so no voter of $G$ can reach $3$. Hence
$t\ge2$.

The four voters $4,5,6,7$ have
$\bigcap_{i=4}^{7}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $|S|=4$.
$S$ is $2$-cohesive and needs a voter in $\{4,5,6,7\}$ with
$\ge2$ approvals in $W$.  Now
$A_{4,5}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$ and
$A_{6,7}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$ are disjoint from $A_{1}$,
so any representative for $\{4,5,6,7\}$ must lie outside $A_{1}$.
With $|W|=5$ and $t=|W\cap A_{1}|$ we need $5-t\ge2$, i.e. $t\le3$,
and $5-t\ge2$ is also necessary for the $2$-cohesive group to be
met.

Hence $2\le t\le3$ is feasible.  For example

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|A_{8}\cap W_{min}|=3$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W_{min}|=2$, so EJR is satisfied;

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|A_{1}\cap W_{max}|=3$ and
$|A_{4}\cap W_{max}|=2$, so EJR is satisfied.

No EJR committee can have $t\ge4$, because then $5-t\le1$ and no
voter $4\!-\!7$ can obtain two representatives, and no EJR committee
can have $t\le1$, because the $3$-cohesive group $G$ would be
unrepresented.  Thus the number of $A_{1}$-candidates in an EJR
$5$-committee can be $2$ and it can be $3$, and nothing else.

Min $2$, Max $3$; i.e. option H.

3.text:
With $n=10,\;k=5$ we have $\ell n/k =2\ell$.  A group $T$ is $\ell$–cohesive
iff $|T|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_{i}|\ge\ell$ and EJR requires
$\exists i\in T\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

The two large cohesive groups are

* $T_{X}= \{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ , $|\bigcap A_{i}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
  $|T_{X}|=6$.  $T_{X}$ is $3$–cohesive and $2$–cohesive.
* $T_{Y}= \{4,5,6,7\}$ , $|\bigcap A_{i}|=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
  $|T_{Y}|=4$.  $T_{Y}$ is $2$–cohesive.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$c={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $d=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$e_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $e_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b+c$.

$T_{X}$ $3$–cohesive $\Rightarrow$ $\exists i\in T_{X}$ $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$.
If $a\ge3$ this is automatic.  If $a=2$ we need $b+c\ge1$ or
$y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}\in W$.  If $a=1$ we need $b=c=1$, i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|
\ge3$.  Hence $a\ge1$ and in particular $a+b+c\ge2$, and $a+b+c=1$ is
impossible.  The $2$–cohesive $T_{Y}$ gives
$\exists i\in\{4,5,6,7\}\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$, i.e. $d+e_{1}\ge2$ for
$i=4,5$ or $d+e_{2}\ge2$ for $i=6,7$.  Hence $d\ge1$ and if $d=1$ then
$e_{1}=1$ or $e_{2}=1$.  In particular $W$ must contain at least one
$y$–candidate.

Hence $|W\cap A_{1}|=p=a+b+c$ satisfies $p+r=5$ with $r$ the number of
non-$A_{1}$ members.  $d\ge1$ forces $r\ge1$, so $p\le4$. $p=4$ would give
$r=1$ and $d=1$, $e_{1}=e_{2}=0$, whence the $Y$-voters obtain only one
approval, contradicting the $2$-cohesive $T_{Y}$.  Thus $p\le3$.

$p=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\}$,

$a=3$, $d=1$, $e_{1}=1$.  Voter $8$ has $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{8}|=4\ge3$ and voter $4$ has $y_{4},z_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $T_{X}$ and $T_{Y}$ are satisfied and all other
cohesive groups are met.  Here $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

$p=2$ is attainable, e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}\}$,

$a=2$, $b=c=0$, $d=2$, $e_{1}=1$.  Voter $8$ has
$x_{1},x_{2},z_{1}$ $=3\ge3$ and voter $4$ has $y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}$ $=3\ge2$,
so EJR holds and $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$.

$p=1$ would need $a=1,\;b=c=0$ or $a=0$, which cannot give a voter of
$T_{X}$ three approvals, so $p\ge2$.  Hence over all EJR committees

$\min |W\cap A_{1}|=2,\qquad \max |W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

i.e. option H.

1.text:
The group $A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $\cap_{i\in A}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and
$|A|=6=3\,n/k$.  Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,   $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}= {\bf 1}_{\{z_{1}\in W\}},z_{2}= {\bf 1}_{\{z_{2}\in W\}},z_{3}= {\bf 1}_{\{z_{3}\in W\}}$,
$y_{1}= {\bf 1}_{\{y_{1}\in W\}},y_{2}= {\bf 1}_{\{y_{2}\in W\}},y_{3}= {\bf 1}_{\{y_{3}\in W\}}$.

$|W|=5$,

$a+y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+c+z_{1}+z_{2}+z_{3}=5$                     (1)

and for voter 1

$w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$ .

EJR for $T_{A}$ with $\ell =3$ gives

$\max \{a+y_{1}+z_{3},\,a+y_{2},\,a+y_{3},\,a+z_{1}\}\ge 3$,       (2)

and for $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\cap T_{B}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|T_{B}|=4=2n/k$,

$\max\{c+z_{1},c+z_{2}\}\ge 2$.                                   (3)

Hence $b:=c+z_{1}+z_{2}\ge2$ is necessary for (3).  From (1)

$w_{1}=5-b-(y_{2}+y_{3})\le5-b$,

so with $b\ge2$ and $y_{2}+y_{3}\ge0$

$w_{1}\le3$,

and $w_{1}=3$ is attainable e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,\;c=2,\;w_{1}=3$,

and (2)–(3) are satisfied with voter 1 approved $3$ times and every
$4$-set in $B$ approved twice.

The smallest possible $w_{1}$ is obtained with $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$,
$a=2$ and $y_{2}=1$ or $y_{3}=1$ or $z_{1}=1$ to meet (2).  With
$b=2$ we can take e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=2,\;y_{2}=1,\;c=2$,
$w_{1}=a=2$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+y_{2}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=c=2$.

Hence an EJR committee can be chosen with $w_{1}=2$ and no EJR
committee can have $w_{1}<2$, since $a\ge1$ is forced by $\{1,8\}$ and
$a=1$ already needs $y_{1}+z_{3}=1$ to reach $3$ in (2).

So $2\le w_{1}\le3$, i.e. the minimum is $2$ and the maximum is $3$.

$H$

8.text:
With $n=10$ and $k=5$ the EJR threshold is $\ell n/k =2\ell$.
For $\ell =3$ we have to look at the $6$-coalitions.

$A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is the $6$–coalition which meets in
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and

* $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
* $A_{2}=A_{3}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{2/3}\}$,
* $A_{8-10}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\}$.

Hence for $S=A$

\[
\max_{i\in A}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3 .
\]

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b_{1}=[y_{1}\in W]$,
$b_{3}=[z_{3}\in W]$, $d=[z_{1}\in W]$.  Then

\[
\max_{i\in A}|W\cap A_{i}|=a+\max\{b_{1}+b_{3},[y_{2}\in W],
[y_{3}\in W],d\}\ge 3 .
\tag{1}
\]

The other $4$-coalition $B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ meets in $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$
and

\[
c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|,\qquad e=[z_{2}\in W],
\]
so that for $\ell =2$

\[
\max_{i\in B}|W\cap A_{i}|=c+\max\{d,e\}\ge 2 .\tag{2}
\]

The six $A$–voters can be made $\ge 3$–represented only with
$a=3$.  Indeed $a\le 2$ would need $b_{1}+b_{3}\ge 1$, $[y_{2}\in W]=1$
and $d=1$ simultaneously, i.e. at least $2+1+1+1=5$ places for the
$A$–part alone, and (2) would then be violated.  Hence $a=3$ is
forced.

With $a=3$ (1) is already satisfied.  From $|W|=5$ we have two places
left.  Condition (2) needs $c+\max\{d,e\}\ge2$, i.e. at least one
$y_{4,5,6}$ together with a $z_{1}$ or $z_{2}$.  The two remaining
places can therefore be used only for the $B$–part.  In particular

\[
b_{1}=b_{3}=0,
\]

so that

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}=3 .
\]

Every EJR committee is therefore of the form

\[
W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}\cup\{u,v\},\qquad
u\in\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\},\;v\in\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ {\rm or}\
|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|=2,
\]

e.g. $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},z_{1}\}$, and

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=3
\]

for every EJR committee.  In particular the $6$-voters obtain the
$3$ proportional seats $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$ and voter $1$ is represented
by exactly those three $x$’s.  Up to the $\ell=5$ inessential
vacuous step this is the usual EJR range, i.e. the essentially unique
EJR value for voter 1 is $3$, min $= $ max $=3$.

This is the $E$ item in the list.

public_text.4:
The $n/k=10/5=2$.  
For a cohesive group $S$ we need $|S|\ge \ell\,n/k$ and
$|\cap_{i\in S}A(i)|\ge\ell$ and then some $i\in S$ has
$|A(i)\cap W|\ge\ell$.

* $S_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\cap A(i)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|S_{x}|=6$.
  $\ell =3$ is cohesive.  Hence some $i\in S_{x}$ has $\ge3$ approvals in $W$.
  $A(2)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{2}\},A(3)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{3}\}$ and
  $A(8\!-\!10)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\}$.  The cheapest way to give a

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The profile has $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.

$T_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_X}A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$, $|T_X|=6$.
$T_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_Y}A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, $|T_Y|=4$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $y_1,z_3$ indicators for voter 1 only,
$y_2,y_3,z_1,z_2$ indicators, $c=|W\cap\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$.
$|W|=5$.

For $T_X$ with $\ell=3$ we need
$\max\{a+y_1+z_3,\;a+y_2,\;a+y_3,\;a+z_1\}\ge 3$.
For $T_Y$ with $\ell=2$ we need
$\max\{c+z_1,\;c+z_2\}\ge2$.

Voter 1 approvals in $W$ are $w_1=a+y_1+z_3$.

$T_Y$ forces at least two places outside $A_1$.  Indeed $A_4,A_5,A_6,A_7$ are
disjoint from $A_1$, so $5-w_1\ge2$ is not sufficient in general but
$c+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$ implies $|W\setminus A_1|\ge2$ and hence
$w_1\le3$.

$w_1=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_1|=1$, impossible for $T_Y$ to obtain
$2$ approvals.  $w_1=3$ is attainable, e.g. 
$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,
$a=3,c=2$, $w_1=3$, $|W\cap A_2|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$.

$w_1=2$ is attainable, e.g.
$W=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$,
$a=2$, $y_2=1$, $c=2$, $w_1=2$, $|W\cap A_2|=a+y_2=3$,
$|W\cap A_4|=c=2$.
Hence the $3$-cohesive $T_X$ is represented by voter 2, not by voter 1,
and $T_Y$ is represented.

$w_1=1$ is impossible: with $w_1\le1$ we have $a\le1$ and
$\max\{a+y_1+z_3,a+y_2,a+y_3,a+z_1\}\le2<3$, so $T_X$ with $\ell=3$ is
violated.  $w_1=0$ is also impossible.

Thus $2\le w_1\le3$ with both bounds tight.  Minimum $2$, maximum $3$,
option H.

Disagreement in round 0: Colleagues 7 and 8 claim $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|\ge3$ is forced and hence $w_1=3$ for every EJR committee. That would require the three $x$’s to be in the committee, i.e. to require the $\ell$-representative of $T_X$ to be taken from the common core. The standard EJR condition only needs a voter in $T_X$ to have $\ge3$ approvals, which can be achieved with $a=2$ together with $y_2$ or $z_1$, as exhibited above. The $2$-place requirement for $T_Y$ is compatible with that.

Current belief is min $2$ max $3$, i.e. H, with the two dissenting $E$ claims being based on an overly strong core-representation requirement.

reflection_text.4:
The profile has $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.

$T_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_X}A_i=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$, $|T_X|=6$.
$T_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_Y}A_i=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$, $|T_Y|=4$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}|$, $y_1,z_3$ indicators for voter 1 only,

$|W|=5$.

For $T_X$ with $\ell=3$ we need
$\max\{a+y_1+z_3,\;a+y_2,\;a+y_3,\;a+z_1\}\ge 3$.
For $T_Y$ with $\ell=2$ we need
$\max\{c+z_1,\;c+z_2\}\ge2$.

Voter 1 approvals in $W$ are $w_1=a+y_1+z_3$.

$T_Y$ forces at least two places outside $A_1$.  Indeed $A_4,A_5,A_6,A_7$ are
disjoint from $A_1$, so $5-w_1\ge2$ is not sufficient in general but
$c+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$ implies $|W\setminus A_1|\ge2$ and hence
$w_1\le3$.

$w_1=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_1|=1$, impossible for $T_Y$ to obtain
$2$ approvals.  $w_1=3$ is attainable, e.g. 
$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}$,
$a=3,c=2$, $w_1=3$, $|W\cap A_2|=3$, $|W\cap A_4|=2$.

$w_1=2$ is attainable, e.g.
$W=\{x_1,x_2,y_2,y_4,y_5\}$,
$a=2$, $y_2=1$, $c=2$, $w_1=2$, $|W\cap A_2|=a+y_2=3$,
$|W\cap A_4|=c=2$.
Hence the $3$-cohesive $T_X$ is represented by voter 2, not by voter 1,
and $T_Y$ is represented.

$w_1=1$ is impossible: with $w_1\le1$ we have $a\le1$ and
$\max\{a+y_1+z_3,a+y_2,a+y_3,a+z_1\}\le2<3$, so $T_X$ with $\ell=3$ is
violated.  $w_1=0$ is also impossible.

option H.

That would require the three $x$’s to be in the committee, i.e. to require the $\ell$-representative of $T_X$ to be taken from the common core. The $2$-place requirement for $T_Y$ is compatible with that.

Current belief is min $2$ max $3$, i.e. H, with the two dissenting $E$ claims being based on an overly strong core-representation requirement.

5.text:
The $6$-set $A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$-cohesive with
$\bigcap_{i\in A}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and the $4$-set
$B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive with $\bigcap_{i\in B}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},z_{1},z_{2},z_{3}\in\{0,1\}$.

Then $|W|=5$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}=:t$,

and EJR gives

$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+z_{1}\}\ge3$,     $\tag{A3}$

$\max\{c+z_{1},c+z_{2}\}\ge2$.                               $\tag{B2}$

From (B2) $c+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$, hence at least two seats are
spent outside $A_{1}$.  With $t=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$,

$5-t=5-a-y_{1}-z_{3}\ge2\Longrightarrow t\le3$,

and $t=4$ would need $5-t=1$, impossible for (B2).  Hence $t\le3$.

$t=3$ is realised e.g. by

$W_{\max }=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

with $a=3,\;c=2,\;|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (A3) and (B2) hold.

$t=2$ is realised e.g. by

$W_{\min }=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

with $a=2,\;y_{2}=1,\;c=2,\;|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+y_{2}=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$.
Thus the $3$-cohesive $A$ is represented by voter 2 and the $2$-cohesive
$B$ is represented by voters 4,5, and EJR is satisfied.

$t=1$ is impossible: with $a+y_{1}+z_{3}\le1$ we have
$a+y_{2}\le2$, $a+z_{1}\le2$, so no voter of $A$ can reach three
approvals, contradicting (A3).  Hence $t\ge2$.

Consequently an EJR $5$-committee can give voter 1 $2$ approvals and can
give voter 1 $3$ approvals, and no other number is possible.

Min $2$, Max $3$, i.e. option H.

Hence $c+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$ and in particular at least two seats of $W$
lie outside $A_{1}$.  With $|W|=5$ this gives $w_{1}=a+p\le3$, and the
$\ell=3$ condition gives $a+\max\{p,y_{2},y_{3},z_{1}\}\ge3$, whence
$a+p\ge2$.  $w_{1}=1$ is impossible and $w_{1}=4$ would leave only one
seat for $S_{Y}$, contradicting $c+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$.

The bounds are tight.

* Max $w_{1}=3$: $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,p=0,c=2$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$.
EJR is satisfied.

* Min $w_{1}=2$: $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,p=0,y_{2}=1,c=2$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+y_{2}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=2$.  The $3$-cohesive $S_{X}$ is represented by voter 2
and the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ is represented by voters 4,5, so EJR holds.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can give voter 1 $2$ approved members and can
give him $3$ approved members, and no EJR committee can give him $<2$ or
$>3$.  This is the $2\le w_{1}\le3$ range, i.e. option H.  The
$a=3$ forced claim of the $E$ minority fails because $a=2$ can be
compensated by $y_{2},y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$ to reach the $3$ requirement for
$S_{X}$ while still leaving $\ge2$ seats for $S_{Y}$.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: H. min 2, max 3

Let $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.  Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $y_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$, $z_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

$|W|=5$ and for voter $1$
$w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$.

$T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|\cap A_{i}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|T_{X}|=6$.
EJR for $\ell =3$ gives

$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},\,a+y_{2},\,a+y_{3},\,a+z_{1}\}\ge 3$,   (1)

$T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|\cap A_{i}|=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$.
EJR for $\ell =2$ gives

$\max\{c+z_{1},\,c+z_{2}\}\ge 2$.                (2)

In particular $b:=c+z_{1}+z_{2}\ge2$ for (2).  From $|W|=5$

$w_{1}=5-b-(y_{2}+y_{3})\le5-b\le3$.

Hence $w_{1}\le3$ and $w_{1}=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,\;c=2$, $w_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$,

so the upper bound is tight.

Lower bound.  If $w_{1}\le1$ then $a+y_{1}+z_{3}\le1$.  With $a\ge0$ this
forces $a\le1$ and $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$.  Then $a+y_{2}\le2$, $a+y_{3}\le2$,
$a+z_{1}\le2$, so (1) cannot be $\ge3$.  Hence $w_{1}\ge2$.

The bound $w_{1}=2$ is attainable.  Take $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$, $a=2$ and meet
(1) with a different member of $T_{X}$, e.g. $y_{2}=1$, $z_{1}=1$ and
$c=2$.  For instance

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2$, $y_{2}=1$, $c=2$, $w_{1}=2$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+y_{2}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=c=2$,

which satisfies (1) and (2).  The same is obtained with
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ giving $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$.

Thus over all EJR 5-committees

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

i.e. minimum $2$ and maximum $3$.  The forcing $a=3$ used by colleagues
7 and 8 requires the three common $x$’s to be in $W$, which is not
required by EJR: with $a=2$ the 3-representation of $T_{X}$ can be
provided by voter $2$, $3$ or $8\!-\!10$ via $y_{2},y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$.
Hence the feasible range is $2\!-\!3$, option H.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: H. min 2, max 3

The 6-voter $X$-cluster $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$-cohesive with
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and the $4$-voter
$Y$-cluster $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive with
$\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $b_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$b_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $y_{2},y_{3},z_{1},z_{2}$ as indicators and
$c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  For voter 1
$w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}$.

$3$-cohesiveness of $S_{X}$ is
$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{3},\,a+y_{2},\,a+y_{3},\,a+z_{1}\}\ge 3$,
$2$-cohesiveness of $S_{Y}$ is $c+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2$, i.e.
$b_{Y}:=c+z_{1}+z_{2}\ge 2$.  Hence $5=|W|=a+b_{1}+b_{3}+y_{2}+y_{3}+b_{Y}$
gives $w_{1}=5-b_{Y}-(y_{2}+y_{3})\le 3$, so $w_{1}\le 3$.

$w_{1}\ge2$.  If $w_{1}\le 1$ then $a\le1$ and
$\max\{a+b_{1}+b_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+z_{1}\}\le2<3$, contradicting the
$3$-cohesiveness of $S_{X}$.  Hence $w_{1}\ge2$.

Both bounds are attainable.  Max:
$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3,c=2$, $w_{1}=3$, $|A_{2}\cap W|=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.

Min:
$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=2,y_{2}=1,c=2$, $w_{1}=a=2$,
$|A_{2}\cap W|=a+y_{2}=3$, $|A_{4}\cap W|=2$.
The $6$-voter $X$-cluster is $3$-represented by voter 2 and the
$4$-voter $Y$-cluster is $2$-represented by voters 4–5, so $W_{min}$ is
EJR and voter 1 receives only the two $x$’s.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can give voter 1 $2$ approvals and can give
him $3$ approvals, and nothing else.  The claim $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|\ge3$
is the common-intersection version of EJR; EJR only requires
$\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$, which is met with $a=2$ and
$y_{2}=1$ or $z_{1}=1$, e.g. the $W_{min}$ above.  So min$=2$, max$=3$, i.e.
option H.

4.text:
The $n/k=2$ threshold gives the two relevant cohesive families

* $T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{X}|=6$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{X}}A_{i}
 =\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, so $T_{X}$ is $3$–cohesive and $2$–cohesive;
* $T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{Y}|=4$, $\bigcap_{i\in T_{Y}}A_{i}
 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, so $T_{Y}$ is $2$–cohesive.

Put 
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$,
$y_{1}= {\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\,z_{3}= {\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$,
$y_{2},y_{3},z_{1},z_{2}\in\{0,1\}$ and $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.
Then

$w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+y_{2}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+y_{3}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+z_{1}$ and
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=c+z_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=c+z_{2}$.

EJR for $T_{X}$ with $\ell =3$ is

$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},\,a+y_{2},\,a+y_{3},\,a+z_{1}\}\ge 3$, \tag{2}

and for $T_{Y}$ with $\ell =2$

$\max\{c+z_{1},c+z_{2}\}\ge 2$. \tag{3}

Hence $c+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$ and with $|W|=5$

$w_{1}=5-\bigl(c+z_{1}+z_{2}+y_{2}+y_{3}\bigr)-a +a
\le 5-2 =3$,
so $w_{1}\le3$ and $w_{1}=4$ would leave at most one seat outside
$A_{1}$, contradicting (3).  In particular $W$ must contain at least two
members of $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.

If $w_{1}\le1$ then $a\le1$ and
$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+z_{1}\}\le2<3$, so (2) is
violated.  Hence $w_{1}\ge2$.

The bounds are attainable.

Maximum.  $W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$a=3,\;c=2,\;w_{1}=3$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=|W\cap A_{8}|=3$ and $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (2)–(3) hold.

Minimum.  $W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$a=2,\;y_{2}=1,\;c=2,\;y_{1}=z_{3}=0$,
$w_{1}=a=2$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+y_{2}=3\ge3$,
$|W\cap A_{4}|=c=2\ge2$ and $|W\cap A_{8}|=a=2\ge2$.
Hence $T_{X}$ is $3$–represented by voter $2$ and $T_{Y}$ is
$2$–represented by voters $4\!-\!7$, i.e. $W_{\min}$ is EJR and
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$.

Thus an EJR $5$–committee can give voter $1$ $2$ approved members and
can give him $3$ approved members, and no EJR committee can give him
$1,0$ or $4,5$ members.  The $a\ge3$ claim of colleagues 7 and 8
confuses EJR with the requirement that the $\ell$ representatives be
taken from the common core $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$; EJR only asks for
the existence of a voter in $T_{X}$ with $\ge3$ approvals, which can be
obtained with $a=2$ together with the private candidate $y_{2}$ or
$z_{1}$.

Min $2$, Max $3$, i.e. option H.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: H. min 2, max 3

8.text:
With $n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$ and a group $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$|S|\ge 2\ell$ and $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge\ell$.
Put  

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$d_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $d_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},z_{3}$ as indicators.

Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}=:w_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=a+y_{2}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=a+y_{3}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=a+d_{1}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}|=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6$ is $3$-cohesive and $2$-cohesive.  Hence

$\max \{a+y_{1}+z_{3},\,a+y_{2},\,a+y_{3},\,a+d_{1}\}\ge 3$,
\tag{2}

$ S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ , $|\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}|=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4$ is $2$-cohesive.  Hence

$\max \{c+d_{1},c+d_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $c+\max\{d_{1},d_{2}\}\ge2$.
\tag{3}

With $|W|=5$ let $b=c+d_{1}+d_{2}+y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+z_{3}\ge2$ be the
number of non-$x$ seats.  Then $w_{1}=5-b-(y_{2}+y_{3})\le5-b\le3$,
so $w_{1}\le3$ and $w_{1}=4$ would give $b\le1$ and contradict (3).

$a=1$ is impossible for (2): $\max\{1+y_{1}+z_{3},1+y_{2},1+y_{3},
1+d_{1}\}\le2$.  Hence $a\ge2$ and $w_{1}\ge2$ with $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$.

The bounds are tight.  

* Max.  $a=3,\;c=2,\;d_{1}=0$,
$W^{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
$|W^{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W^{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W^{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$.
(2)–(3) hold and $w_{1}=3$.

* Min.  $a=2,\;y_{2}=1,\;c=2$,
$W^{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
$|W^{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W^{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+y_{2}=3$,
$|W^{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented by voter $2$
and $S_{Y}$ is $2$-represented by voter $4$.  The same $w_{1}=2$ is
obtained e.g. with $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ where voter $8$
gives the $3$-representation of $S_{X}$.

Hence an EJR $5$-committee can give voter $1$ $2$ approved members and
can give him $3$ approved members, and no EJR committee can give him
$<2$ or $>3$.  That is $\min w_{1}=2$, $\max w_{1}=3$.

Option H.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: H. min 2, max 3

Let $n=10,k=5$, $n/k=2$. Put
$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$y_{v}={\bf1}_{y_{v}\in W}$, $z_{j}={\bf1}_{z_{j}\in W}$.

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$, $w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{X}}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6$.  $S_{X}$ is $3$-cohesive and $2$-cohesive, so EJR needs

$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},\,a+y_{2},\,a+y_{3},\,a+z_{1}\}\ge 3$         (2)

and in particular $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge2$ for some $i\in S_{X}$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_{Y}}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4$.  $S_{Y}$ is $2$-cohesive, so

$\max\{c+z_{1},c+z_{2}\}\ge2$, i.e. $b:=c+z_{1}+z_{2}\ge2$.      (3)

$|W|=5$ gives $w_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+b=5$ up to the $a$–overlap, hence
$w_{1}=5-b-(y_{2}+y_{3})\le5-b\le3$ by (3).  $w_{1}=4$ would give
$5-w_{1}=1$, so $b\le1$ and (3) would be violated.  Hence $w_{1}\le3$.

$w_{1}=3$ is EJR-realizable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$a=3,\;c=2$, $w_{1}=3$,
$|A_{1}\cap W_{\max}|=3$, $|A_{2}\cap W_{\max}|=3$,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\max}|=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$-represented and $S_{Y}$
is $2$-represented.

$w_{1}=2$ is EJR-realizable.  Take $a=2$, $y_{1}=z_{3}=0$, $y_{2}=1$,
$c=2$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$w_{1}=a=2$, $|A_{2}\cap W_{\min}|=a+y_{2}=3$, so (2) holds for voter 2,
$|A_{4}\cap W_{\min}|=c=2$, so (3) holds for $S_{Y}$.  The same is
obtained with $z_{1}$ in place of $y_{2}$, e.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ with $|A_{8}\cap W|=3$.

$w_{1}=1$ is impossible.  With $w_{1}=1$ we have $a+y_{1}+z_{3}=1$, so
$a\le1$.  Then
$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+z_{1}\}\le a+1\le2<3$,
contradicting the $3$-cohesive requirement for $S_{X}$.  Hence
$w_{1}\ge2$.

Thus over all EJR $5$-committees

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with the two bounds attained.  This is option H, min $2$, max $3$.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: H.  min 2, max 3

Let $n=10$, $k=5$, $n/k=2$.
Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}}$.
For $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ we have $\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6$, so $S_{X}$ is $3$–cohesive and $2$–cohesive.  With
$y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,

$\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|
      =\max\{a+{\bf1}_{y_{1}}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}},\;a+y_{2},\;a+y_{3},\;a+z_{1}\}\ge 3$,

and for $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ $\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4$, $S_{Y}$ is $2$–cohesive, with $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,

$\max\{c+z_{1},c+z_{2}\}\ge2$.

Hence $b:=c+z_{1}+z_{2}\ge2$ and $|W|=5$ gives $w_{1}=5-b-(y_{2}+y_{3})
\le5-b\le3$.  The $Y$–condition also forces $5-w_{1}\ge2$, i.e. $w_{1}\le3$,
and $w_{1}=4$ would leave only one seat outside $A_{1}$ and can give a
$Y$–voter at most one approval, so $w_{1}\le3$.

The $3$–cohesive condition is met with $a=2$.
E.g. $W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$a=2$, $w_{1}=2$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=a+y_{2}=3$ and
$|W\cap A_{4}|=|W\cap A_{5}|=c=2$, $|W\cap A_{6}|=|W\cap A_{7}|=c=2$.
Hence $S_{X}$ is $3$–represented by voter 2 and $S_{Y}$ is $2$–represented
by voters 4–7.  So $w_{1}=2$ is attainable and $w_{1}\ge2$ is necessary,
for $a=1$ gives $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.

The upper bound is attainable, e.g.
$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$a=3$, $w_{1}=3$, $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8}|=3$
and $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$.
Thus over all EJR $5$-committees

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with the two extremes realised.  This is the $2\!-\!3$ range, option H.
The $a\ge3$ forcing claimed by Colleagues 7–8 fails because the $\ell=3$
requirement on $S_{X}$ can be satisfied by voter 2 with $a+y_{2}$ or by
voter 8 with $a+z_{1}$, so $a=2$ together with $y_{2}=1$ or $z_{1}=1$ is
EJR-feasible.

public_text.5:
The $6$-set $A=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ is $3$-cohesive with
$\bigcap_{i\in A}A_{i}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and the $4$-set
$B=\{4,5,6,7\}$ is $2$-cohesive with $\bigcap_{i\in B}A_{i}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
Put

$a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$, $c=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$,
$y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},z_{1},z_{2},z_{3}\in\{0,1\}$.

Then $|W|=5$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}=:t$,

and EJR gives

$\max\{a+y_{1}+z_{3},a+y_{2},a+y_{3},a+z_{1}\}\ge3$,     $\tag{A3}$

$\max\{c+z_{1},c+z_{2}\}\ge2$.                               $\tag{B2}$

From (B2) $c+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$, hence at least two seats are
spent outside $A_{1}$.  With $t=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$,

$5-t=5-a-y_{1}-z_{3}\ge2\Longrightarrow t\le3$,

and $t=4$ would need $5-t=1$, impossible for (B2).  Hence $t\le3$.

$t=3$ is realised e.g. by

$W_{\max }=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

with $a=3,\;c=2,\;|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{2}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (A3) and (B2) hold.

$t=2$ is realised e.g. by

$W_{\min }=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

with $a=2,\;y_{2}=1,\;c=2,\;|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{2}|=a+y_{2}=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4}|=2$.
Thus the $3$-cohesive $A$ is represented by voter 2 and the $2$-cohesive
$B$ is represented by voters 4,5, and EJR is satisfied.

$t=1$ is impossible: with $a+y_{1}+z_{3}\le1$ we have
$a+y_{2}\le2$, $a+z_{1}\le2$, so no voter of $A$ can reach three
approvals, contradicting (A3).  Hence $t\ge2$.

Consequently an EJR $5$-committee can give voter 1 $2$ approvals and can
give voter 1 $3$ approvals, and no other number is possible.

Min $2$, Max $3$, i.e. option H.
public_text.7:

$\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=\max\{c+z_{1},c+z_{2}\}\ge2$
for the $\ell=2$ cohesive $S_{Y}$.

Hence $c+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$ and in particular at least two seats of $W$

and the $2$-cohesive $S_{Y}$ is represented by voters 4,5, so EJR holds.

 =\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, so $T_{Y}$ is $2$–cohesive.
